method: Commit-level review of each commit separately. Gate fix reviewed directly. Feature reviewed by two independent read-only reviewers (SQL migration and probes; TypeScript routes, libraries and Edge functions), then every finding was verified against the source and dispositioned. Remediations were applied on the branch in a follow-up commit and re-gated.

findings.claim: COL-133 policies on audit_log_export_jobs reference row_count; Finance alters that column's type; PostgreSQL refuses ALTER TYPE on a column used in a policy
findings.verified: reproduced on the scratch cluster: ERROR cannot alter type of a column used in a policy definition
findings.disposition: Recorded as a hard ordering constraint in migration-reconciliation.json: Finance's export migration must apply before COL-133's authority migration (the rehearsed Finance-first order applies cleanly). If COL-133 ever lands first, the integrator must drop and recreate operation_export_job_current and operation_export_job_insert_current around Finance's ALTER. No branch file changed.
Already resolved by the proposed reconcile migration and proven by its probe (finance-integration/resolution.json).

findings.where: export job lifecycle and org-wide scope differ between branches
findings.disposition: Resolved in the reconcile: single snapshot lifecycle (COL-133 completion RPC revoked from authenticated); org-wide scope uses the intersection (Finance owner/org_admin rule AND COL-133 current grant). Open integration decision recorded: COL-133 hides completed jobs from the requester's list while Finance's UI expects to list them; retrieval remains authority-checked so relaxing the list policy for snapshot-bearing completed jobs would lose no protection, but that is the integrator's call, not made here.

findings.claim: no SQL probe for user_facility_access.revoked_at or operation_subject_access.revoked_at (only in the Python concurrency script outside the replay)
findings.disposition: Fixed: two cases added (revoked site grant hides task_a and denies completion even with no expiry; revoked subject grants hide the resident and personnel tasks). Replay PASS.

findings.claim: meeting/card audit rows hidden regardless of linkage; template, activity and aggregate audit rows hidden entirely
findings.disposition: Accepted as the conservative contract boundary for this segment; narrowing to linked rows is a follow-up once link metadata is reliable in old_data/new_data. Recorded, no change.

findings.claim: org-wide (facility NULL) templates become unwritable and invisible to humans; legacy templates with now-foreign links cannot be retired via publication
findings.disposition: Consistent with the spec (explicit facility typing). Added to the handoff's compatibility boundaries. Recorded, no change.

findings.where: restrictive read policies calling VOLATILE definer helpers per row
findings.claim: list queries pay repeated actor lookups per row
findings.disposition: Performance follow-up; correctness unaffected. Recorded, no change.

sql_review.finance_overlap: Shared tables audit_log and audit_log_export_jobs; no object-name collision; Finance's guard trigger permits COL-133's definer update. Edge function on the merged tree calls materialize_audit_export/retrieve_audit_export; haven_complete_audit_export_job is superseded.

findings.claim: create_meeting_action is revoked by 337:509, so the route always failed at the RPC with a generic 'retry' 409 after reading the meeting
findings.disposition: Fixed: explicit 409 'Meeting task creation requires a classified command and is not available yet' returned after actor and body validation, before any meeting read or RPC; tests rewritten around the unavailable path (success-path tests retained in history at afe24111).

findings.claim: the database always rejects escalate, yet the route took the task and authority locks first and returned a 409 inviting retries
findings.disposition: Fixed: explicit 409 returned after authentication, before revalidation, locks or RPC; test asserts no revalidation or RPC call.

findings.claim: Edge accepted failed jobs the completion RPC rejected (generic 500 after reading every page); final scope check ran after the job was already completed, which could strand a completed job with no bytes
findings.disposition: Fixed: completion RPC now accepts pending, processing and failed; the single current-authority assertion runs after the bytes are built and before the completion command, whose locked recheck is the last gate. Tests updated; two negative tests added (missing current site grant, different requester).

findings.claim: raw PostgreSQL error messages returned in the HTTP body
findings.disposition: Fixed: fixed strings returned; detail kept in structured logs.

findings.claim: one unclassified legacy task halts scoring for every organisation processed after it, with nondeterministic organisation order
findings.disposition: Not changed. COL-133 deliberately fails the whole service run closed when its restricted projection disagrees with the raw population; continuing per organisation would label partial coverage as complete. Recorded as an owner decision for the operating release (deterministic ordering is a cheap follow-up).

findings.where: assets, vendors, maintenance-templates, start and reinstate routes
findings.claim: no route tests exercise actorCanAccessFacility denial there
findings.disposition: Partially addressed (export and escalate). Route-level negative tests for the remaining surfaces are a follow-up; the guard itself is covered by auth.test.ts.

findings.where: complete/defer 404 vs task-command 403 for hidden tasks
findings.disposition: Both hide existence; unified status is a follow-up.

findings.where: facilities routes ignore risk_score_snapshots read errors (null readiness)
findings.disposition: Accepted; null is the safe display value.
